name: session-band
description: Prompt-cache countdown, cost to re-warm, usage limits, cold-cache warnings and one-click handoff → clear & continue.

cacheTtl.title: Prompt-cache TTL
cacheTtl.description: auto: 1h on a subscription, 5m otherwise, corrected by what the API actually served after a gap

warnMinutes.title: Warn this many minutes before the cache goes cold
warnMinutes.description: A toast and a band above the prompt appear once the countdown drops below this

inputPricePerMTok.title: Base input price, USD per million tokens (0 = auto)
inputPricePerMTok.description: auto calibrates from the session's own cost ledger, falling back to list price

autoCompact.title: Auto-compact point for every session
autoCompact.description: auto: 300k tokens on 1M-context models, 70% of smaller windows (never below 100k). Or off, or a token count like 250k. A session can override it from the details pane or with /session-band autocompact <250k|off|auto>

handoffCommand.title: Slash command the Handoff button runs
handoffCommand.description: A skill or command name without the slash; when missing, a built-in handoff prompt is sent instead

saveCommand.title: Slash command the 📝 Save notes button runs
saveCommand.description: Skill or command that updates your project's working notes, without the slash; empty or missing sends a built-in prompt instead

statusPrompt.title: Prompt the 🧭 Status button sends
statusPrompt.description: Asks where the work stands; empty sends a built-in English prompt

compactInstructions.title: Instructions passed to every compaction
compactInstructions.description: Sent as /compact's argument by the 📦 button and by auto-compact; empty uses Claude Code's default summary
compactInstructions.default: Keep: (1) the goal and why; (2) decisions made and their reasons, rejected alternatives; (3) touched file paths, commands, IDs, URLs and version numbers verbatim; (4) current state: what is done, what is verified, what is half-done; (5) remaining work and the next step; (6) corrections and style preferences the user gave. Drop: raw tool output dumps, file contents already read and concluded on, details of failed attempts (keep only "X did not work, because Y"), repeated explanations. Mark anything uncertain with "?"; do not invent.

styleRules.title: Writing rules the ASD toggle switches on
styleRules.description: Attached to every prompt while the toggle is on, and exclusive with caveman; empty hides the toggle. The default is a summary of the tr-sade-teknik-dil skill (Turkish and English)
styleRules.default: Sade teknik dil (the rules of the tr-sade-teknik-dil skill). Apply them to all prose you write for the user: replies, reports, document text. Leave code, commands, quoted text and names as they are. Use the rules of the language you are writing in. (1) One action or claim per sentence. (2) Turkish: at most 18 words per sentence. English: at most 25. (3) Active voice with the actor as subject. Keep a passive only when the actor is unknown or irrelevant. (4) Simple tenses: no "-mektedir", "-mış bulunmaktadır", "yapmış olduğu"; no English present perfect. (5) No semicolons. (6) No "olup" and no converb chain (-ıp, -arak, -dıktan sonra) joining actions: split the sentence. (7) A verb, not a noun plus an empty verb: "incele", not "incelemesini gerçekleştir". (8) Plain words: no officialese ("işbu", "tarafınıza", "akabinde"), no idiomatic verbs ("ayağa kaldır", "göz at"), no marketing adjectives. (9) One verb for one action, used the same way throughout. (10) No dropped subject, object or verb. (11) Three or more steps or conditions go in a list. Keep every fact, condition, scope limit and number. Keep each hedge exactly as strong as it is ("olabilir", "muhtemelen", "may"). Keep the longer form when a shorter one loses precision. Do not announce or mention these rules.

styleSkill.title: Skill the ASD writing rules belong to
styleSkill.description: The toggle shows only while this skill is installed (name without the slash); empty shows it whenever rules are set
